plans.note: Limitation of liability / consequential damages waiver is normally housed at the end of the indemnity article (sec-11-2) in this deal form; check for mutuality, any monetary cap, and carve-outs (confidentiality, IP infringement, willful misconduct). Miscellaneous (sec-13-2) is a secondary location.

Article 11 should contain reciprocal indemnities; confirm Harpoon (Licensor) indemnifies us for third-party IP claims arising from the Licensed Compound and its Harpoon In-License/Existing Patents, and that AbbVie Indemnitees coverage is not narrower than Harpoon Indemnitees coverage.

Defined terms 'Segregate', 'Competitor' and 'Other Product' signal a competing-product/exclusivity restriction on AbbVie, most likely in the grant-of-rights article (sec-5-2) with development/commercialization hooks in sec-3-2/sec-4-2. Assess scope, duration and whether it binds our Affiliates.

Exclusive licence in our favour is beneficial and should not be flagged; look only for reverse obligations restricting AbbVie from sourcing or developing alternative BCMA/Delivery System products (sec-5-2, sec-4-2).
No MFN/best-terms concept appears in the definitions or payment headings; if anything exists it would sit in Article 6 (payments, royalty reductions at sec-6.5.3) or the grant article. Expect absent.
No employee non-solicit is signalled in the outline; if present it would be a miscellaneous covenant (sec-13-2) or bundled with confidentiality (sec-9-2).

Article 12 should contain termination at will (typically AbbVie's right to terminate on notice) plus Harpoon's for-cause rights; verify our convenience right has no penalty and that Harpoon has no mirror convenience termination.
Term likely runs to expiry of the Royalty Term rather than an auto-renewing subscription term; check sec-12.1 for any evergreen/renewal mechanic before concluding absent.

Governing law, dispute escalation to Senior Officers and forum/arbitration provisions sit in Article 13; confirm law is New York/Delaware/California/England & Wales and that disputes go to courts rather than foreign arbitration.

Assignment/successors clause expected in Article 13; test our ability to assign to Affiliates and in an Acquisition, and whether Harpoon gains termination or altered rights on AbbVie's change of control (see 'Acquisition', 'Divestiture', 'Voting Stock' definitions).

Article 7 governs ownership of AbbVie Know-How/Patents, Joint IP and Product-Specific Patents; confirm AbbVie retains ownership of its own inventions and data and that AbbVie Reversion IP assignments on termination are not broader than necessary.
Check the Article 5 grant for Affiliate and Sublicensee/Third Party Provider coverage, irrevocability during the Term, and that any grant-back to Harpoon is limited.
Records and audit rights against AbbVie (royalty/Net Sales audits, Audit Expert) live in Article 6; test frequency, notice, scope and who bears cost absent a material underpayment.
No liquidated damages/penalty concept flagged; watch for interest on late payments or penalty-style payments on termination in Articles 6 and 12, which are ordinarily acceptable.

Article 10 contains mutual reps plus Harpoon covenants (sec-10.3) and AbbVie covenants (sec-10.4); assess Harpoon's IP/non-infringement, in-licence compliance and no-debarment warranties and any disclaimer of implied warranties.
Insurance obligations, if any, would follow the indemnity provisions in Article 11; no separate heading suggests it may be absent in this development/option structure.
Milestones and royalties (Articles 6, 6.2.4, 6.3.1) are success-based, not take-or-pay; only flag if Article 3/4 imposes a minimum spend or guaranteed purchase volume on AbbVie.

Consequences-of-termination in Article 12 should cover reversion (Harpoon Reversion Products, AbbVie Reversion IP, Terminated Territory) and transfer of Regulatory Documentation/data; also check Manufacturing Technology Transfer obligations referenced in Article 3.
